key_insight: MDTransformer proposes a hardware-software co-design for photonic Transformer acceleration that reduces reliance on expensive multi-wavelength sources and large dot-product units. It uses a mode-division photonic architecture with an inverse-designed coherent crossbar to make Transformer inference more efficient and practical.
problem_solved: Current photonic Transformer accelerators are limited by costly light-generation requirements and bulky, inefficient dot-product hardware built around active phase-shifters, making them hard to scale and deploy.
method: Designs a mode-division photonic Transformer accelerator to improve hardware efficiency.
Introduces an inverse-designed coherent crossbar to support compact and scalable optical computation.
Co-optimizes hardware and software to better match Transformer inference workloads with photonic circuitry.
impact: This work could make photonic AI acceleration more realistic for high-throughput, energy-efficient Transformer inference. For practitioners, it points to a path toward faster inference hardware with lower power and potentially better scalability than conventional photonic designs.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison of conventional photonic Transformer accelerators vs. MDTransformer

paper_title: MDTransformer: A Hardware-Software Co-Design of Mode-Division Photonic Transformer Accelerator with Inverse-Designed Coherent Crossbar
paper_authors: Solomon Micheal Serunjogi, Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Ayat Taha, Muhammad Shafique, Mahmoud Rasras
